q: 1. If d1 is the depth of cutting, d2 is the height of the bank... the horizontal distance n between the bed and bank, is .............
explain: The horizontal distance depends on the slope ($r$) and the height ($d$) of the bank; hence $x = r_2 \times d_2$.

q: 2. Finally formed berms in canals are provided for .............
options: protection of banks erosion by the waves
explain: Berms act as a buffer, reducing wave impact, providing space for sediment to settle (which seals the banks), and widening the bank base for stability.

q: 3. The saturation line is the line up to which banks get saturated after the canal runs for some time. The saturation gradient in ordinary loam soil, is generally .............
explain: In ordinary loam, the phreatic line (seepage line) usually follows a gradient of 4 horizontal to 1 vertical.

q: 4. A counter berm is .............
options: a horizontal benching provided on the inside slope
a horizontal benching provided on the outside slope
a vertical benching provided on the outer edge of the bank
a vertical benching provided on the inner edge of the bank
explain: A counter berm is added to the outside of a canal bank to keep the saturation line well within the body of the bank, preventing leaks.

q: 5. A minimum of 90 cm free board is provided if the discharge in the canal is between .............
explain: Freeboard increases with discharge capacity. For large canals (>60 cumecs), 90 cm (0.9m) is standard.

q: 6. The width of a dowla is generally kept between 30 to 60 cm and its height above the road level should invariably be more than .............
explain: A dowla is a small protective ridge on the edge of the service road. A height of 30 cm is required for safety and to prevent runoff into the canal.

q: 7. If straight sides of a triangular section of a lined canal with circular bottom of radius R, make an angle θ with horizontal, the area of its cross-section, is .............
explain: Based on the geometric properties of a standard triangular canal section with a rounded bottom, the area $A = R^2 (\theta + \cot \theta)$.

q: 8. If the straight sides... make an angle θ with horizontal, the perimeter of the canal is .............
explain: For the same rounded triangular section, the wetted perimeter $P = 2R (\theta + \cot \theta)$.

q: 9. If the straight sides of a triangular section of a lined canal with circular bottom of radius D, make an angle θ with horizontal, the hydraulic mean depth is .............
explain: For a triangular section with a rounded bottom, the hydraulic mean depth (Area/Perimeter) simplifies to R/2 (or D/2 if D is the radius).

q: 10. An outlet which maintains a constant discharge irrespective of fluctuation in the water levels of supplying channel or water course, is known as .............
explain: Rigid modules (like the Gibb's module) are designed to provide a fixed discharge regardless of the water levels in the parent canal or the field channel.

q: 11. A fall in a canal bed is generally provided, if .............
options: ground slope exceeds the designed bed slope
designed bed slope exceeds the ground slope
ground slope is practically the same as the designed bed slope
explain: When the natural ground falls more steeply than the required canal bed slope, a 'fall' or 'drop' structure is built to step the water down safely.

q: 12. In concrete canal the approximate permissible velocity of water should not exceed .............
explain: Concrete lining can withstand higher velocities without erosion; the typical upper limit to prevent damage is around 2 to 2.5 m/sec.

q: 13. The sensitivity of a rigid module, is .............
explain: Sensitivity is the ratio of change in outlet discharge to change in canal level. Since a rigid module's discharge is constant, its sensitivity is zero.

q: 14. A current meter measures the velocity of flow, if it is held .............
options: at any point within the cross-section
explain: Current meters are versatile instruments designed to measure local flow velocity at any specific depth or horizontal position in a channel.

q: 15. If the height of the hydraulic gradient line above the floor of thickness l is h and the specific gravity of the material of the floor is G, the minimum thickness t of the floor downstream of the crest is given by the equation .............
explain: The floor thickness must counter the uplift pressure. The formula $t = (h-1)/(G-1)$ ensures the weight of the concrete balances the net upward force.

q: 16. Bligh's theory of seepage assumes .............
options: equal weightage to the horizontal and vertical creep
more weightage to horizontal creep than vertical creep
less weightage to horizontal creep than vertical creep
loss of head following the sine curve
explain: Bligh's Creep Theory famously makes no distinction between horizontal and vertical creep paths regarding head loss.

q: 17. For the design of major hydraulic structures on the canals, the method generally preferred is based on .............
explain: Khosla's method is the modern standard because it accounts for the actual flow net and the influence of various floor components independently.

q: 18. The ratio of the discharge over a trapezoidal crest to a rectangular crest of Sarda falls of identical parameters, is .............
explain: A trapezoidal crest has a slightly higher discharge coefficient due to its shape, resulting in a ratio of approximately 1.084 compared to a rectangular crest.

q: 19. In a Sarda type fall, the rectangular crest, may be used for discharge upto .............
explain: Rectangular crests are efficient for lower discharges; once the discharge exceeds 14 cumecs, a trapezoidal crest is usually preferred.

q: 20. In Montague type fall .............
explain: Montague falls use a parabolic glacis to ensure the water profile follows the structure closely, increasing energy dissipation efficiency.

q: 21. To hold hydraulic jumps, baffle walls are provided in .............
explain: The English (or Baffle) fall uses a specific wall on the floor to stabilize the hydraulic jump and dissipate energy.

q: 22. Bed bars in a canal are provided .............
options: to watch the general behavior of canal
explain: Bed bars are masonry or concrete strips built across the canal bed at intervals to serve as permanent benchmarks for monitoring siltation or scour.

q: 23. In a canal siphon, the flow is .............
explain: In a siphon, the canal is enclosed in a barrel and flows full under pressure, similar to flow in a pipe.

q: 24. The uplift pressure on the roof of an inverted siphon, is maximum when .............
explain: The maximum upward force on the roof occurs when the drainage (which is above the siphon barrel) is at its Highest Flood Level.

q: 25. The main function of a diversion head works of canal from a river, is .............
explain: The primary role is to raise the river's water level (pond level) so that water can flow into the off-taking canal by gravity.

q: 26. The depth of the crest of a scouring sluice below the crest of a head regulator, is generally kept .............
explain: A difference of 1.2 meters is standard to allow for a 'silt pocket' where heavier sediment can settle and be flushed out.

q: 27. The crest level of a canal diversion head work, depends upon .............
explain: The crest level of the weir is dictated by the required pond level needed to feed the canal at its Full Supply Level.

q: 28. Retrogression of the bed level of a river downstream a weir, occurs due to .............
explain: When clear water (silt-free) is discharged over a weir, it has high capacity to pick up sediment, causing the downstream bed to scour or retrogress.

q: 29. According to Lacey, depth of scour in a river depends upon the straightness of the reach. If D is the depth of scour in regime flow in a right angled bend, it is .............
explain: Lacey suggested multipliers for scour depth based on river curvature; for sharp right-angled bends, the scour depth is taken as 2.0 times the normal regime depth.

q: 30. According to Khosla, the exists gradient of surface flow .............
options: is independent of the b/d ratio
is independent of the depths of d/s cut off walls
explain: Exit gradient depends on the ratio of floor length (b) to the depth of the downstream end pile (d).

q: 31. The width of a meander belt is the transverse distance between .............
options: apex point of one curve and apex point of the reserve curve
explain: Meander belt width is the total width of the valley occupied by the river as it swings from one extreme apex to the other.

q: 32. The length of a meander is the distance along the river between the tangent point of one curve to the tangent point of .............
options: next curve of the same order
reverse curve plus the width of the river
explain: Meander length is measured as the axial distance between two corresponding points (like consecutive crests) on the same side of the meander.

q: 33. Process of meandering is due to .............
options: discharge and hydraulic properties of streams
relative erodibility of the bed and banks
explain: Meandering is the result of excess energy in the flow interacting with erodible banks and varying sediment loads.

q: 34. A river is said to be of .............
options: aggrading type if it builds up its bed
degrading type if it cuts its bed
meandering type if it flows in sinuous curve
explain: These are the three primary morphological classifications of alluvial rivers based on their bed-level trends and planform.

q: 35. A deficit of sediments in flowing water may cause a river .............
explain: If the water has less sediment than its carrying capacity, it will scour the bed to pick up more, leading to 'degradation'.

q: 36. The downstream expansion head of a guide bank is extended to subtend an angle at the center, equal to .............
explain: For efficient flow expansion downstream, a guide bank is usually curved with an arc subtending 45 degrees.
